records.wording: NA27 (checked on the page image, p. 208).
records.reason: Class U?: The man with dropsy healed on the sabbath (14:1–6) and the places at table (14:7–11): two NA27 paragraphs with no attested verse (METHOD §4.3). Tertullian passes from 13:28 (4.30.6) to 14:12 (4.31.1); his "rursus" at 4.30.1 introduces 13:15 (the ox or donkey watered), not 14:5 (the son or ox in a well). Restored by method (METHOD §11): by its words, the printed text needs the passage. 14:12 "he said also to the one who had invited him (τῷ κεκληκότι αὐτόν)" takes up 14:10 "the one who invited you (ὁ κεκληκώς σε)"; the printed text has no host and no meal since 11:37. 14:15 "those reclining with him (συνανακειμένων)" takes up 14:10, and "eat bread" takes up 14:1. By its mechanics: 14:7–14 is one teaching about the meal; the printed text has the host's half (call those who cannot repay) without the guest's half (take the last place and be called up higher, to glory). Reading: docs/research/correspondence/word_by_word.md, chapter 11, test of 14:1–11.

witnesses.evidence: "qui scilicet humanitatis istius vicem retribuere non possint. Hanc si Christus captari vetat, in resurrectione eam repromittens…"

records.wording: NA27. Tertullian has "in the resurrection" without "of the righteous"; the words are not quoted, and no omission is attested (Roth). Printed.

records.reason: A one-verse NA27 paragraph, but part of the attested pericope: the parable 14:16–24 is the answer to it ("But he said to him").

witnesses.evidence: "Etiam invitatoris parabola cui magis parti occurrat expende. Homo quidam fecit coenam et vocavit multos."

records.wording: NA27. Tertullian does not have "great"; Roth: "μέγα may have been present". Printed.

witnesses.evidence: "Dehinc si is mittit ad convivas qui coenam paravit…"

witnesses.evidence: "Agrum emi, et boves mercatus sum, et uxorem duxi."

witnesses.evidence: "Hoc ut patrifamiliae renuntiatum est, motus tunc (bene quod et motus, negat enim Marcion moveri deum suum…) mandat de plateis et vicis civitatis facere sublectionem."

records.wording: NA27. Tertullian's "motus" ("moved") is rated possible only as a rendering of a different verb (Roth: ἐπαρθείς?); NA27 ὀργισθείς is printed.

witnesses.evidence: "praecepit etiam de viis et sepibus colligi, id est nos iam de extraneis gentibus".

records.reason: Hating one's family and carrying the cross (14:25–27), the tower and the king at war (14:28–33), and salt (14:34–35): three NA27 paragraphs with no attested verse. Epiphanius refers to 14:26 in a refutation (Pan. 42.11.17, ἔλ. 70), but not as a reading of Marcion's text (Roth). Tertullian passes from 14:24 (4.31.8) to 15:4 (4.32.1).
